text:
```yaml
name: CLI Publish

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  build-and-test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v3

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v3
        with:
          node-version: '14'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Run tests
        run: npm test

      - name: Upload test coverage to Codecov
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v2
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          files: ./coverage/lcov.info
          flags: unittests
          name: codecov-umbrella
          fail_ci_if_error: true

  deploy:
    needs: build-and-test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'

    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v3

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v3
        with:
          node-version: '14'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Build packages
        run: npm run build

      - name: Deploy to production
        run: |
          echo "Deploying to production..."
          # Add your deployment commands here
```

This GitHub Actions workflow file `.github/workflows/cli-publish.yml` includes two jobs:

1. **build-and-test**: This job runs when changes are pushed to or opened as a pull request against the `main` branch. It sets up Node.js, installs dependencies, runs tests, and uploads test coverage to Codecov.

2. **deploy**: This job runs after the `build-and-test` job succeeds and only when changes are pushed to the `main` branch. It sets up Node.js, installs dependencies, builds the packages, and then deploys them to production. You will need to add your actual deployment commands in the `Deploy to production` step.
